review_notes: I read the whole file: the SiegelSlab lemmas, the local archUnit/finUnit definitions, and the final `solution` theorem. The only candidate was `archUnit`/`finUnit`, which build the units (d.1, 1) and (1, d.2) of the product adele ring. Mathlib has `MulEquiv.prodUnits : (M × N)ˣ ≃* Mˣ × Nˣ` (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Prod.lean). `archUnit` and `finUnit` could be written as `prodUnits.symm` applied to a pair with 1 in one slot. They are small local helpers, not a competing concept. Writing them via a generic map would not make the named helpers redundant. The cost of keeping them is also small: I found no duplicated API or repeated conversions. A search of the repo found no other definition with the same names. The other results were different declarations (`archUnitHom`, `finUnitIdele`, `archUnitsBorel`). I did not check whether `AdeleRing` is definitionally a product in a way that would make `prodUnits` convenient. The remaining lemmas (`det_fst_apply`, `det_snd_eq`, `archDetNorm_eq`, `ideleNorm_det_eq_prod`) are theorem-level statements, which are excluded from this rubric. I found no avoidable competing version of a Mathlib concept, so I report none_found.
